title: Columbus warns residents about official-looking email scam requesting money
text:
Columbus | wikipedia.org
Columbus | wikipedia.org
The City of Columbus and the Columbus Police Department have issued a warning about an ongoing email scam targeting residents. According to officials, the scam involves detailed emails that appear legitimate, using City branding and information sourced from public records. The messages often impersonate the mayor or use the name "City of Columbus," with requests for recipients to wire money.
Officials stress that neither the City of Columbus nor its staff or elected officials will ever request money transfers through unsolicited emails. Payments for city services such as bills, permits, or taxes should only be made through official City websites or in person at City offices. The city does not reach out unexpectedly to ask for funds.
The advisory provides several tips to help residents avoid falling victim to these scams:
- Confirm the sender's email address; official communications from city staff, council members, and the mayor will come from addresses ending in @columbuswi.gov. Utility and library departments have their own domains listed on their respective official websites.
- Be cautious with subject lines that seem urgent or threatening, as these are common tactics used by scammers.
- Watch for spelling and grammatical mistakes in messages. While some scams are poorly written, others may appear more convincing.
- Avoid clicking on links or opening attachments unless you specifically requested them; scammers may use these to direct users to fake websites or install malware.
- Never wire money or buy gift cards to pay for any city service—the City of Columbus does not require such payment methods.
Residents who suspect they have received a fraudulent email claiming to be from the city are encouraged to contact the Columbus Police Department directly.
